turns.text: I have type 1 diabetes and I've had a stomach bug since yesterday and can't keep food down. What are the sick-day rules I should be following right now?
Why does my glucose go up when I'm ill even though I'm not eating? I'd like to understand what's happening.
How do I adjust the mealtime insulin when I'm eating almost nothing, while keeping the basal going?
If I could reach my diabetes team, what numbers would they ask for and what would they be deciding?
What do diabetes nurses recommend sipping when you're vomiting — sugary or sugar-free, and how often?
A friend with type 1 says she sets an alarm every two hours through the night when she's sick. Is that what I should do?
Someone else said flat lemonade in small sips is the trick when nothing stays down. Is there anything better?
My clinic is closed for the weekend and I've no ketone strips. What can I do without them, and where could I get some today?
Exactly which signs mean I stop managing at home and go to hospital?
Could you write out a sick-day plan for the next 48 hours — insulin, testing, fluids, and the go-to-hospital rules?
